Subject: Severe 5xx/429 bursts across regions — immediate attention needed

Hi Grace,

We started seeing a huge spike of 502/503 responses and 429 throttles across our traffic this morning (US-East + EU-West + APAC edge). Timeouts on several customer-facing endpoints, and our frontend is repeatedly retrying which is making the backend error rate even worse. Attached are sampling logs and a screenshot from our monitoring.

Impact: our checkout calls are failing ~18% for the past 20 minutes, latency has gone from ~120ms to >2s for many requests. We are seeing downstream LB 502/503 and backend timeouts.

Can Redwood take an immediate look? We need status, mitigation, and an ETA.

Thanks,
Tim Reilly
Engineering Lead, Acme Retail

On Fri, Mar 20, 2026 at 8:20 AM, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai wrote:
> Forwarding the alert from Acme.

Initial triage: we're seeing correlated 429 bursts and backend 502/503s in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 on the regional edge. Traffic graphs show sharp client retry patterns around 08:05-08:15 that align with the spike.

What we've done so far:
- Scoped the error buckets: ~60% 429 (rate limiting), ~30% 502/503 LB errors, ~10% internal timeouts.
- Confirmed no config pushes in the last 24h that would explain it.
- Suspect a combination of client retry loops plus an overloaded regional LB pool that started evicting backends.

Short-term mitigation plan (now -> +1h):
1) Apply temporary token-bucket throttle for heavy Acme routes at the edge to reduce retry amplification.
2) Enable fallback routing: shift ~30% traffic from us-east to eu-west for non-latency critical paths.
3) Reduce LB retry attempts (client side) for Acme to avoid cascading retries.
4) Open a scoped circuit breaker for the affected model endpoint to give backends breathing room.

Assigning: Marissa to run quick metric pulls and apply throttles; I'll coordinate routing changes and LB rules. Grace: please deliver an immediate status to the customer that we are applying mitigations and will follow up.

-Sean
SRE Lead

Subject: Re: Fwd: Customer: Acme Retail - 5xx/429 bursts (multi-region) — metric dump + next steps

Attaching logs and a couple of quick dashboards (see acme-logs-us-east-03-20.tar.gz). The load pattern shows sustained bursts from a handful of client IP blocks that correlate with aggressive retry logic in their SDK.

Notes:
- Edge LB in us-east started showing 502 and 503 when active backend pool dropped below 40% healthy due to concurrent requests.
- We see a retry loop from their frontend that replays at 100-200 qps per instance; combined it's producing a retry storm.
- Quick mitigation applied: token-bucket throttle (10 rps per token) on the top 5 routes, reduced LB retry attempts from 3->1 for the Acme route.

Recommendation (short): enable global client-side retry backoff and ask Acme to patch SDK to exponential backoff. If they cannot, we'll keep the edge throttle and maintain routing split.
